subject: part
title: PART.------HI.P.
description: First of two diagrams on page 437 (MP(I)-11). The crossing diagrams how participation structurally meets high-purpose at the activist-creativity scale: PART (participation — actual creative participation in the form) is crossed with HI-P (high purpose — the cultural-political high-purpose participation is supposed to serve). PART sits on the left with the subject-arrow; AF-DY (affinity dynamics) hangs at the left margin as the subject's leftward output. UNF-PI (unified physical-implication) rises at the upper-right and TR (transformation) sits below it, with OBS (observation) and HI-P clustered at the partner-axis center-right. IF-ST-DY (isolated-focus stable-dynamics) sits centrally with CULT-O (cultural other) below it and MT-INFO (meta-information) at the lower-left as subject-side downward outputs. RIT-DY (ritual dynamics) hangs at the right with P-FC (political-focus / functionalism) below as partner-side downward outputs, and MTA-RT-SIGN (meta-reality signal) at the bottom-center as the bridging-axis terminus. Structural argument: when participation is crossed with high-purpose, the upper diagonal UNF-PI → TR → OBS → HI-P is the *high-purpose route* — unified-physical-implication routes through transformation into observation and into high-purpose. The subject's downward chain IF-ST-DY → MT-INFO is what participation produces on its own without the partner-axis: isolated-focus stable-dynamics into meta-information. The central CULT-O → RIT-DY → P-FC → MTA-RT-SIGN chain is the bridging-axis: cultural-other routes through ritual-dynamics into political-focus and finally into meta-reality signal at the bottom. AF-DY on the subject's left margin is what affinity-dynamics provides as participation's actual working ground. The argument structurally: participation reaches high-purpose only when the upper diagonal holds all four edges *and* the central bridging chain holds; otherwise participation produces only meta-information (subject-side) or meta-reality signal (bridging-side), without ever crossing into the partner-axis's working high-purpose.
